faq_heading: Coquitlam West condos and townhomes: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Coquitlam West. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Coquitlam West, Coquitlam: 359 condos and townhomes listed at the end of September 2026 and 35 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 10%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. By listings that is number 1 of 23 Coquitlam communities for condos and townhomes.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Coquitlam total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Listings of condos and townhomes in Coquitlam West fell from 390 in June to 359 in September (−7.9%), and 178 sold across the 4 months. In September the community held 44.5% of Coquitlam’s 806 condos and townhomes listed.
Condos and townhomes or houses in Coquitlam West?
Coquitlam West also had 76 houses listed and 2 sold in September, against 359 condos and townhomes listed. The Coquitlam West houses page has those figures.

blocks.text: Coquitlam West home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

389 condos sold in Coquitlam West with a median price of $620,000 (the middle half sold between $509,900 and $728,000), taking a median of 27 days to sell at 97.5% of the last list price; 7% sold above list. They had a median $835 per square foot, a median year built of 2021 and a median strata fee of $393 a month. 46 townhomes sold in Coquitlam West with a median price of $938,950 (the middle half sold between $799,225 and $1,024,975), taking a median of 36 days to sell at 99.0% of the last list price; 7% sold above list. They had a median $749 per square foot, a median year built of 2023 and a median strata fee of $423 a month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Coquitlam West
567 Clarke & Como — 567 Clarke Road

A 49-storey, 364-unit concrete strata high-rise built in 2021 by Marcon, steps to Burquitlam SkyTrain Station; current listings describe over 20,000 sq ft of amenities including concierge, fitness centre, sauna, sports courts, guest suites and a 49th-floor Sky Lounge, with full air conditioning. Published rental/pet/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked — confirm on the Form B.
Lougheed Heights — 657 Whiting Way
Strata plan EPS4093; a 37-storey, 597-unit concrete strata high-rise built in 2019 by Bosa Properties. Published rental/pet/age restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Marquee at Lougheed Heights — 652 Whiting Way

Strata plan EPS4095; a 29-storey, 242-unit concrete strata high-rise built in 2020 by BlueSky Properties (a current listing credits Bosa as the renowned developer behind the Lougheed Heights project — the developer attribution differs between sources; the strata plan and form are not in dispute). Listings describe 17,000 sq ft of amenities including a fitness centre, outdoor pool, party room and dog walk. Published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Precidia Lougheed — 699 Whiting Way

A 29-storey, 178-unit concrete strata high-rise built in 2024 by Ledingham McAllister; current listings describe it as rising 29 storeys in the heart of West Coquitlam, steps to SkyTrain, shops and dining, with pets recorded as "Cats OK" on one listing. Other published restrictions: UNCONFIRMED.
Elements at Burquitlam — 628 Whiting Way
The directory page checked published no rental/pet/age restriction lines: restrictions UNCONFIRMED. Tower/low-rise form and construction: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
The Burquitlam Capital — 691 North Road

Built 2019; a concrete freehold strata tower, strata plan EPS5721 — one building source records 193 homes in 23 storeys, while the developer records 189 condominiums plus four townhomes and approximately 10,500 sq ft of commercial space (the counts differ by source and are both stated here; the strata plan governs). The developer places it 200 metres from Burquitlam Station. Amenities in listings: rooftop garden with BBQ, gym, lounge and EV charging. Published rental/pet restrictions: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Brookside Manor — 515 Whiting Way

Built 1993 (building directory, secondary source). The directory records restrictions as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed with restrictions, and lists amenities as elevator, garden, in-suite laundry, storage and wheelchair access. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED — the directory's own unit-count field is internally inconsistent, so no count is published here. Construction: UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked.
Streets, schools and getting around Coquitlam West

items.t: Coquitlam West is the City of Coquitlam's south-west side; the City plans the same ground as Southwest Coquitlam, covering the neighbourhoods around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre SkyTrain stations and along Austin Avenue. Exact MLS sub-area boundary lines are UNVERIFIED — the City describes the planning area by its station areas and the Austin Avenue corridor, not by boundary roads.
Main roads serving the area: North Road, Clarke Road, Austin Avenue and Lougheed Highway; Burnaby (Lougheed / Cariboo) sits across North Road to the west and Central Coquitlam to the east.

Where the condo stock concentrates: almost entirely at the two station nodes — the Whiting Way / Clarke Road tower cluster between Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre stations (567 Clarke & Como, Lougheed Heights, Marquee, Precidia, Elements at Burquitlam, Brookside Manor) and the North Road tower at Burquitlam Station (The Burquitlam Capital). The Austin Avenue and interior streets remain freehold houses.

At the Coquitlam community level that month, condos & townhomes posted a median sale price of $625,000, $687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list and 23 days on market (SnapStats GVR September 2026 report — community-level figures only; SnapStats publishes no sub-area medians).
Transit anchors: Burquitlam Station (Millennium Line, Evergreen Extension) and Lougheed Town Centre Station (Millennium and Expo Lines).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Coquitlam West

items.t: Watercourse permit area: a Watercourse Protection Development Permit can be required for land within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam, with Zoning Bylaw s. 519 flood-protection setbacks and s. 523 riparian rules behind it — relevant to strata capital planning in slope-side buildings.

blocks.text: Good to know about Coquitlam West

items.t: Two sources give The Burquitlam Capital two different sizes. A building source records 193 homes in 23 storeys (strata plan EPS5721); the developer records 189 condominiums plus four townhomes — 193 homes in total, counted differently. The strata plan, not either marketing count, governs unit entitlement and fees.

A third station-area district is already in presale. Burquitlam Park District, by Intergulf at Clarke Road and Como Lake Avenue, is planned in two phases: 40- and 33-storey condo towers with 663 strata homes in phase one, a further 213 market condominiums in a 27-storey tower in phase two, plus a rental apartment tower and a 5-storey non-market rental building, with completion estimated for 2028 (presale-directory source, secondary). The rental components are not strata condos and are not counted in.

The City renamed the ground under the towers. The same station areas the MLS calls Coquitlam West are planned by the City as Southwest Coquitlam, and the Transit-Oriented Areas Update plus Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments were adopted following a public hearing — planning documents and listing copy using older area names are describing the same stations.
Detached and strata moved in opposite directions in September 2026.

The newest tower was completing during the research itself. Elements at Burquitlam (628 Whiting Way) is dated 2026 by the building directory with no units listed for sale on that page at crawl time — early resales there are effectively new-build purchases for GST and warranty purposes until the facts of the specific unit say otherwise.

Streets, schools and getting around Coquitlam West

items.t: Coquitlam West is the GVR board sub-area name for the City of Coquitlam's south-west side; the City plans the same ground as Southwest Coquitlam — the neighbourhoods around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre SkyTrain stations and along Austin Avenue. Exact sub-area boundary lines: UNVERIFIED (the City describes Southwest Coquitlam by its station areas and the Austin Avenue corridor, not by boundary roads).
Nearby areas: Central Coquitlam to the east, Maillardville to the south-east, Port Moody to the north-west, and Burnaby (Lougheed / Cariboo) across North Road to the west.
Roads: North Road, Clarke Road, Austin Avenue and Lougheed Highway. Stations: Burquitlam (Millennium Line, Evergreen Extension) and Lougheed Town Centre (Millennium and Expo Lines).

Coquitlam community "Condos & Townhomes" COMBINED median was $625,000 in September 2026 ($687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list, 23 days on market) — cited exactly as the report states it, never as a townhome-only figure; no sub-area median is published.

Schools: SD43 catchments are address-based. For the sample address 575 Poirier Street (Coquitlam Public Library Poirier branch), the SD43 locator returns Parkland Elementary, École Montgomery Middle and Centennial Secondary; Burquitlam-side addresses can feed different schools — check the exact address. School names use Ministry-listed names only.

Library and care: Coquitlam Public Library Poirier branch, 575 Poirier Street, is in this part of the city (City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way, serves Coquitlam as a whole); Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, is the Fraser Health hospital on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Coquitlam West

items.t: Form B diligence (The Gable, the counted strata): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

Watercourse setbacks: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers land within 30 metres of the top of bank of any watercourse; Zoning Bylaw s. 519 / s. 523 set flood and riparian setbacks.

Presales (REDMA) — Komo: a presale buyer must receive the developer's disclosure statement (REDMA s. 18) and has a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing or acknowledging it (REDMA s. 21), with deposits in trust. Assignment consent and fees are contract terms: UNCONFIRMED until the Komo disclosure statement is read.

blocks.text: Good to know about Coquitlam West

items.t: Coquitlam replaced its OCP in 2026 (dated fact): Council adopted the Interim Official Community Plan (Bylaws 5511/5512, 2026) on April 27, 2026, superseding OCP No. 3479, as a streamlining foundation for a fuller update anticipated to begin in 2027. Any page still citing OCP No. 3479 as current is out of date.

Edgar Avenue holds both ends of the townhouse story on one street: The Gable (688 Edgar Avenue, 2008 strata townhouses) and Allison by Mosaic (708 Edgar Avenue, 2024 apartment building whose garden unit is marketed as "townhome-like") — same builder family, same street, opposite tenure documents. The listing adjective is not the form; the title is.

Detached and strata moved in opposite directions in the same month (September 2026): a 3% sales ratio for houses against 10% for condos & townhomes — a house seller here is pricing into the slower of the city's two markets, whatever the tower cranes suggest.

The townhouse supply story here is a planning document, not a building: the Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments were adopted to create townhousing opportunities around the two stations and Austin Avenue — the next named townhouse complexes in this sub-area will come from that amendment map, and a lot's position inside or outside it is the first diligence question.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Coquitlam West?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 359 condos and townhomes listed in Coquitlam West. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Coquitlam West a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Coquitlam West had a sales ratio of 10%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Coquitlam West from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 178 condos and townhomes sold in Coquitlam West over those 4 months, out of 475 in all of Coquitlam.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in Coquitlam West sell for?
faq.a: 389 condos sold in Coquitlam West between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $620,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Coquitlam West?
faq.a: The median was 27 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.5% of the last list price (7% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Burquitlam or Lougheed — where is each tower, actually?
faq.a: Both station areas sit inside this one sub-area: The Burquitlam Capital (691 North Road) is at Burquitlam Station, and the Whiting Way / Clarke Road cluster (Lougheed Heights, Marquee, Precidia, Elements, Brookside Manor, 567 Clarke & Como) sits between Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre stations — a current Marquee listing describes that position expressly.

faq.q: How new is the condo stock here?
faq.a: Almost all of it is 2019 or later concrete: Lougheed Heights and The Burquitlam Capital (2019), Marquee (2020), 567 Clarke & Como (2021), Precidia (2024) and Elements at Burquitlam (2026).

faq.q: Can I rent out a unit in these towers?
faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable province-wide since November 24, 2022. Brookside Manor's directory line reads "rentals allowed with restrictions," which predates or sits alongside that change; what can still bind you is a short-term rental bylaw.

faq.q: What did condos do in September 2026?
faq.a: SnapStats publishes no sub-area median, so there is no verified Coquitlam West median price.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Whiting Way or Clarke Road condo?
faq.a: School District 43 catchments are address-based and SD43 is a three-tier district. Run the building's exact address in the SD43 locator before relying on any school claim.

faq.q: Where are the actual townhouses in Coquitlam West?
faq.a: One verified standalone complex: The Gable by Mosaic, 688 Edgar Avenue — freehold-strata townhouses, built 2008 on the majority listing figure. Everything else townhouse-shaped in the sub-area is a component: 4 townhomes inside The Burquitlam Capital strata, townhome units inside The Austin tower, and 4 townhomes in the Komo presale.

faq.q: Is a Burquitlam Capital townhome a different purchase than a tower unit?
faq.a: No — same strata corporation (EPS5721, built 2019), same Form B document set, same bylaws.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Gable townhouse long-term?
faq.a: A strata bylaw cannot bar it — rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw, and The Gable's published restriction set is UNCONFIRMED until the Form B package is read.
